item.title: Perspectives: Scandals, suits have plagued ‘U’ basketball
item.description: As the University of Minnesota men’s basketball team marks 30-, 40- and 50-year anniversaries of major scandals, new coach Niko Medved faces a daunting rebuild.

item.title: Attorney Madel drops GOP governor bid, cites ICE surge
item.description: Republican gubernatorial candidate Chris Madel ends his Minnesota campaign, calling ICE operations unconstitutional and an “unmitigated disaster.”

item.title: Trump, Walz signal possible ICE pullback; judge hears state case
item.description: President Trump signals a possible pullback of the Minnesota immigration crackdown as a federal judge weighs whether she can halt the operation.

item.title: First social media addiction lawsuit heads to trial
item.description: The first social media addiction lawsuit against Meta, TikTok and YouTube goes to trial, testing claims that platform design harms teens’ mental health.

item.title: Quandaries & Quagmires: Public discipline and the unlawful marketing fee
item.description: Rule 5.6(a)’s main policy purpose is to allow clients choice of counsel without migrating counsel being unduly economically disincentivized to continue representation at a new firm.

item.title: CLE to address lawyers’ mental health in turbulent times
item.description: The ACS Minnesota Lawyer Chapter announced an in-person mental health CLE to help attorneys manage stress, trauma, and substance use risks.

item.title: Federal judge threatens ICE acting director with contempt
item.description: U.S. District Chief Judge Patrick Schiltz ordered ICE’s acting director to appear in court and explain repeated failures to comply with immigration detention orders.

item.title: What businesses should know about ICE worksite visits
item.description: As immigration enforcement expands in Minnesota, an attorney explains what businesses should know about ICE visits, warrants, audits, and workplace rights.

item.title: States push laws allowing civil rights suits against ICE agents
item.description: Democratic-led states seek laws allowing civil rights lawsuits against ICE agents as DOJ challenges Illinois law under the Constitution’s Supremacy Clause.

item.title: Court of Appeals upholds reckless threat conviction
item.description: The Minnesota Court of Appeals upheld a conviction for reckless threats of violence, rejecting claims that angry statements were protected speech.
